I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is what I know best, it fits my well irrigation, and at my age with only one person in the household I need a system I can manage steadily. I will put 8.1 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2.0 mu in cotton so I still have some cash crop income without making the whole farm too labor-heavy. I will use better seed on all three crops because I want stable emergence and yield, but I will not push inputs too hard; I would rather aim for steady output than chase a very high yield and take more risk on cost, weather, or pests. For wheat I will fertilize a bit more because it responds well on my land and I can irrigate it several times. For maize I will use hybrid seed, moderate-to-high nitrogen, and fewer irrigations than wheat because summer rain helps. For cotton I will keep the area small, use moderate fertilizer, and spray more times because insects are usually the bigger problem there. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to handle and suits my scale.
